chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Tamattu' and there is not with him what he could buy a sacrificial animal (hady) with. So when he fasts three days during the Hajj, he becomes financially able (easier). Should he buy a sacrificial animal and sacrifice it, or should he leave that and fast seven days when he returns to his family? He (peace be upon him) said: He should buy a sacrificial animal and sacrifice it, and the fasting which he had fasted becomes optional (nafl) for him.

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who performs Tamattu' but cannot afford the sacrifice until after fasting three days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation to sacrifice a hady in Tamattu' Hajj is tied to one's financial capacity at the time of the act, not merely the initial inability to pay. Consequently, if a pilgrim fasts three days while poor and later becomes wealthy, he must still offer the sacrifice, rendering the earlier fasts as voluntary (nafl) rather than the compensatory fidya. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of the compensatory fast depends on the specific condition of 'inability to find' (istita'ah) at the moment of fulfillment.
